# Nova Tools roadmap

<!-- Generated from docs/roadmap.sexp by tools/roadmap. Do not edit this file: edit docs/roadmap.sexp and run `make roadmap`. -->

1.0.0 is the first release of nova-tools. It is cut from `main` when the set below is solid: every tool is tested, its documentation describes it as it is (docs/CLI.md), and every friend has audited 1.0.0 on `main` at the candidate sha and given a last review OK. A green CI run alone is not that bar. The 1.0.0 set is fifteen tools, and nothing outside it ships in 1.0.0: nova-bus (messages and replies between friends, over git); nova-cairn (session notes: explicit checkpoints, source pointers and a bounded index); nova-check (broken links, branch hygiene and other problems in your records); nova-ci (packages over the test-time budget, and ci-ok's run receipt); nova-config (the permanent configuration in Postgres, applied into Redis); nova-fuse (a recorded decision to stop reading a source); nova-memory (matching sources from your Markdown records); nova-redis (the Redis store: `serve` runs it, `spill` and `recall` keep scratch with a TTL, `fn load` puts this binary's function library on it and `fn check` compares without changing anything); nova-sandbox (filesystem restrictions for a command); nova-secrets (encrypted storage, and selected credentials delivered to a child command); nova-self-talk (flagged sentence patterns in how you write about yourself); nova-table (tables over Redis, every cell an ordered set, and their live views); nova-tokens (token usage by model and repository, with gaps shown); nova-update (declared versions checked, and one chosen update applied); nova-version (installed tool identities). The items below are planned work after 1.0.0: open sprint cards moved out of the stopped sprint on 2026-10-14, each naming its card, its tier, its base branch and any pushed work to resume from.
